They are a speed bump for casual abuse, not a wall: someone determined can
come from many addresses, and on hosts whose proxy adds the real address to
the end of `X-Forwarded-For` rather than replacing the header (Cloudflare
documents that it does, and many cloud proxies do the same), can put a
made-up address at the front, which is the entry the server reads. Caddy and
the nginx block above replace the header, so behind them it holds.
new:
They are a speed bump for casual abuse, not a wall: someone determined can
come from many addresses. What they cannot do is pick their address: a
visitor can start `X-Forwarded-For` with anything they like, so the server
reads the **last** entry — the one your proxy added — never the first. Behind
Cloudflare you can name its own header instead with `proxyHeader:
"cf-connecting-ip"` (or `TERRAGLIDE_PROXY_HEADER=cf-connecting-ip`); only do
that behind Cloudflare, because anyone can send that header to a server that
is not.

old: | `trustProxy` | `false` | Read the player's address from the first entry of the `X-Forwarded-For` header (or Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP` when there is no `X-Forwarded-For`). Without it, behind a tunnel or proxy every player looks like the proxy — `127.0.0.1` for a tunnel on the same machine — and they all share one set of rate limits and bans. Turn on **only** behind a tunnel or reverse proxy; directly on the internet it would let anyone claim any address. |
new:
| `trustProxy` | `false` | Read the player's address from what the proxy reports — the **last** entry of `X-Forwarded-For`, the one the proxy added, or `proxyHeader` if set. Without it, behind a tunnel or proxy every player looks like the proxy — `127.0.0.1` for a tunnel on the same machine — and they all share one set of rate limits and bans. Turn on **only** behind a tunnel or reverse proxy; directly on the internet it would let anyone claim any address. |
| `proxyHeader` | `""` | With `trustProxy` on, a header your proxy names the visitor in, which then wins over `X-Forwarded-For` — `"cf-connecting-ip"` behind Cloudflare. Leave it empty anywhere else: a header your proxy does not set, anyone can send. |

old: | `TERRAGLIDE_TRUST_PROXY` | `trustProxy` | `1` for on, `0` for off. **Any value other than `0` means on** — even `false`. |
new:
| `TERRAGLIDE_TRUST_PROXY` | `trustProxy` | `1` for on, `0` for off. **Any value other than `0` means on** — even `false`. |
| `TERRAGLIDE_PROXY_HEADER` | `proxyHeader` | e.g. `cf-connecting-ip`. |

Press `K` (or **Play online** in the toolbar) and press **Play on the public
server** — the one everybody plays on together — or type another server's
address. Every player signs up with a username and a password the first time
and signs in after that;

old:
- **What they have discovered.** In the players list (`Tab`) tick *trail* or
  *discovered* next to anyone — or *everyone* — to draw their trail and the
  ground they have uncovered on your maps, in their colour.
new:
- **What everybody has discovered, on one map.** Ground anyone on the server
  has explored is uncovered on your maps too, with a faint wash over the parts
  you have not been to yourself — on from the start (*Settings → Online →
  Everyone's discoveries*). Paths are lines in each player's colour: tick
  *Everyone's paths*, or *trail* / *discovered* next to anyone in the players
  list (`Tab`) to see just theirs.
- **Friends.** Press *Friend* next to someone in the players list, or type
  their name in the box at the bottom of it, or `/friend add name`. You hear
  when friends come online and go, and can let them teleport to you and pull
  you into their party without asking (*Settings → Online*). A request sent
  to somebody offline waits for them.
- **Parties.** Press *Party* next to someone, or `/party invite name`: up to
  eight of you, with a leader. A party talks on voice however far apart its
  members are — on another world too, like a radio when they are out of
  earshot — has its own chat (`/pc message`), its own **waypoints** (*Mark
  here for the party* in the players list, or *Party waypoint at centre* on
  the world map; they show on every member's maps and compass), and a tick,
  *teleport with the party*: when the leader teleports, travels to another
  world or presses *Gather the party*, everyone with it ticked comes along.
  `/party leave`, `/party kick name`, `/party leader name`, `/party list`.

/**
 * The public server: the one everybody plays on together unless they choose
 * another. The Online panel offers it first, as one button.
 *
 * Its socket address — wss://your-app.fly.dev/ws, say — once it is running;
 * see HOSTING.md, "The public server". The GitHub Pages build fills it in
 * from the repository variable TERRAGLIDE_PUBLIC_SERVER, so it can be set
 * without touching the code. Empty means there is none yet, and the panel
 * asks for an address instead.
 */
export const PUBLIC_SERVER = '';
